label: copy phase, fed-back input t or k (recall_idx >= 3)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only on repeated tokens (in_first == 0). It never fires in the original phase or on <DEL>, and almost never at recall_idx <= 2. The input token matters most: fed-back t (10.5x lift, 41% of mass) and k (6.8x, 23%) dominate, with weaker j and n. Rates are highest in long sequences (L=9 holds 52% of mass), peaking at t=12 (recall_idx 3 when L=9) and at the final step of L=9. The strongest activations are fed-back t at recall_idx 3 in L=9 sequences. Precision is low: most copy-phase t/k inputs stay below threshold, so position and context gate the response in a way this predicate does not capture. About 37% of activation mass falls on other tokens (j, n, r, g, y, ...).
